newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February consumer prices up 2.03 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February consumer prices up 2.03 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's February consumer price index rose 2.03 percent compared to February 1996, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Wednesday.
February's wholesale price index was down 3.22 percent compared to February 1996, the directorate said.
February's consumer price index rise was somewhat lower than an average forecast of 2.54 percent compiled from Tuesday's Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.

The CPI rise was well below the central bank's full-year 1997 inflation forecast of 3.31 percent and an official 1997 CPI target of 3.0 percent set by the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development.

Economists interviewed for the Reuters Poll had said they expected stable consumer price growth in February due to steady food and raw material prices and because of the high comparative base in February 1996, when CPI grew an annual 2.72 percent.
Economists said an average nine percent increase in energy prices implemented with state approval on January 1 was being reflected in consumer prices only gradually.
